content.comment_body: Hello, I am working with a [product_name] using two [product_name] expansion modules. I have connected a 4-20mA sensor to the I1 analog input of one of these expansion modules. My question is: Since the base module already provides multiple analog inputs (I1, I2, I7, I8), does the expansion module assign I1 as AI5 and I2 as AI6?

This depends on the current configuration. The numbering of analog inputs in the expansion module starts after those used in the base module. For example, if you use four in the base module, the expansion module inputs begin at AI5.

The addresses assigned to the analog inputs of the first analog expansion module are determined by the I/O settings for the base module. In the configuration software, under File > Offline Settings > I/O settings, you can see how many addresses are reserved for the base module. Reserved addresses for the base module aren't available for expansion modules, regardless of whether you use the base module's analog inputs. By default, AI1 and AI2 are reserved for the base module. If zero addresses are reserved for the base, the first analog expansion module uses AI1 and AI2; if two addresses are reserved, it uses AI3 and AI4; if four addresses are reserved, it uses AI5 and AI6.

Thank you for your explanation. I disabled analog inputs on the base module, so the first expansion module starts with AI1. If I enable four analog inputs on the base module, then I1 on the expansion module becomes AI5. Best regards, [user_name]
Has your issue been resolved now?

analysis.insight_summary: Users were uncertain about how analog input addresses are assigned when using [product_name] expansion modules with a [product_name] base module. The assignment of addresses (AI1–AI6) is determined by configuration software settings, especially how many addresses are reserved for the base module. This created some confusion regarding proper sensor connections and addressing.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want straightforward and reliable mapping of analog input addresses on expansion modules, depending on the configuration of the base module.
